name: Anaerobic sludge digestion (mesophilic/thermophilic)
principle: Standard published practice: thickened sludge is heated and held 15-25 d (mesophilic, ~35 C) or 8-12 d (thermophilic, ~55 C) in complete-mix digesters where methanogens convert volatile solids to biogas (~60% CH4); optional thermal hydrolysis (Cambi/CNS) pretreatment raises biogas yield and dewaterability; digestate is dewatered and the biogas drives CHP or upgrading.

process_steps.name: Biogas use
equipment: CHP engines or upgrading to biomethane

costs.metric: capital cost, two-stage anaerobic digestion system, 12 MGD plant (Grand Island, Nebraska)
costs.basis: EPA 832-F-06-031 COSTS section: a USD 10.7 million two-stage anaerobic digestion system in design for a 12 MGD plant receiving about 40 percent industrial agricultural flow. Figure published 2006; no dollar year stated.

source.note: US EPA, Biosolids Technology Fact Sheet: Multi-Stage Anaerobic Digestion, EPA 832-F-06-031, COSTS section (named facilities)

costs.metric: capital cost, two-stage TPAD anaerobic digestion system, 43 MGD plant (WLSSD Duluth)
costs.basis: Same section: the WLSSD two-stage TPAD system at a 43 MGD regional plant, in operation from 2001, had a construction cost of USD 32.6 million. Figure published 2006; no dollar year stated.

source.note: US EPA, Biosolids Technology Fact Sheet: Multi-Stage Anaerobic Digestion, EPA 832-F-06-031, COSTS section (named facilities)
